title: Window Functions
tagline: frame clauses, NTILE, percentiles, frame exclusion

options: ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
RANGE UNBOUNDED PRECEDING TO CURRENT ROW
placementQuiz.explain: Default = RANGE UNBOUNDED PRECEDING TO CURRENT ROW. Includes all rows up to current row.

placementQuiz.q: ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING includes:
placementQuiz.explain: 1 PRECEDING = 1 row before; 1 FOLLOWING = 1 row after. Total 3 rows.
NTILE(n) divides rows into n buckets as equally as possible. Buckets numbered 1..n.

placementQuiz.q: EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW in frame clause:
placementQuiz.explain: EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW omits current row from frame. Useful for 'other rows' calculations.

placementQuiz.q: RANGE vs ROWS with ORDER BY salary:
options: RANGE uses value proximity; ROWS uses row count
ROWS uses value; RANGE uses count
placementQuiz.explain: RANGE uses ORDER BY value + offset (e.g., salary ± 1000). ROWS uses physical row count.

blocks.md: Frame = window boundaries. ROWS = physical row count. RANGE = ORDER BY value + offset. Default = RANGE UNBOUNDED PRECEDING TO CURRENT ROW. Always specify frame for LAST_VALUE, running totals, moving averages.

blocks.label: frame syntax
blocks.code:
-- ROWS: physical row count
SUM(amount) OVER (
  ORDER BY sale_date
  ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
) AS moving_sum_4days

-- RANGE: value-based (ORDER BY must be numeric/date)
SUM(amount) OVER (
  ORDER BY sale_date
  RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '3 days' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
) AS moving_sum_3days

-- Unbounded
SUM(amount) OVER (
  ORDER BY sale_date
  ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
) AS total_so_far
blocks.py-pandas:
# Rolling window
df['amount'].rolling(4).sum()  # 4-row window

# Date-based
from pandas import Timedelta
df.set_index('sale_date')['amount'].rolling(Timedelta('3D')).sum()

before.meaning: Current row + rows with ORDER BY value within 3

items.q: RANGE INTERVAL '1 day' PRECEDING with ORDER BY ts includes:
options: All rows where ts >= current_ts - 1 day
items.explain: RANGE uses value semantics. All rows with ts within 1 day of current row's ts.

items.q: ROWS 1 PRECEDING vs RANGE 1 PRECEDING with ORDER BY salary:
options: ROWS = 1 row before; RANGE = salaries within 1 of current
items.explain: ROWS counts rows. RANGE uses ORDER BY value difference (salary ± 1).

blocks.label: ntile
blocks.code:
-- Quartiles (4 buckets)
SELECT 
  name,
  salary,
  NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY salary) AS quartile
FROM employees;

-- Deciles (10 buckets)
SELECT 
  name,
  salary,
  NTILE(10) OVER (ORDER BY salary) AS decile
FROM employees;

-- Per department
SELECT 
  dept_id,
  name,
  salary,
  NTILE(4) OVER (PARTITION BY dept_id ORDER BY salary) AS dept_quartile
FROM employees;
blocks.py-pandas:
# Quantile bins
df['quartile'] = pd.qcut(df['salary'], 4, labels=[1,2,3,4])

# Per group
df['dept_quartile'] = df.groupby('dept_id')['salary'].transform(lambda x: pd.qcut(x, 4, labels=[1,2,3,4]))

blocks.md: NTILE distributes rows as evenly as possible. If rows % n ≠ 0, first buckets get 1 extra row. NTILE(4) on 10 rows → buckets: 3,3,2,2 rows.

items.explain: Extra rows go to first buckets. 10/4 = 2 remainder 2 → first 2 buckets get 3 rows.

items.q: NTILE with PARTITION BY dept_id — buckets per partition:
items.explain: NTILE respects PARTITION BY — each partition gets its own buckets 1..n.

blocks.label: exclude current row
blocks.code:
-- Sum of OTHER employees' salaries in same dept
SELECT 
  name,
  salary,
  SUM(salary) OVER (
    PARTITION BY dept_id
    ORDER BY salary
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
    EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW
  ) AS sum_other_salaries
FROM employees;

-- Exclude group (all tied peers)
SUM(salary) OVER (
  PARTITION BY dept_id
  ORDER BY salary
  RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
  EXCLUDE GROUP
) AS sum_other_tiers

-- Exclude ties
SUM(salary) OVER (
  PARTITION BY dept_id
  ORDER BY salary
  RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
  EXCLUDE TIES
) AS sum_other_tiers
blocks.py-pandas:
# Total minus current
total = df.groupby('dept_id')['salary'].transform('sum')
df['sum_others'] = total - df['salary']

blocks.label: groups frame
blocks.code:
-- GROUPS: counts groups of peer rows (same ORDER BY value)
-- 1 group = all rows with same ORDER BY value
SELECT 
  salary,
  COUNT(*) OVER (
    ORDER BY salary
    GROUPS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING
  ) AS peer_count
FROM employees;

-- Useful for: percentile buckets with variable row density

-- GROUPS frame (PostgreSQL 14+)
-- Counts peer groups (ties) not individual rows
blocks.py-pandas: # No direct equivalent; use rank + transform

items.explain: Excludes only the current row from frame calculation. Other rows with same ORDER BY value remain.

items.q: GROUPS 1 PRECEDING with ORDER BY salary:
options: All rows with same salary as previous distinct salary
All rows with salary less than current
items.explain: GROUPS counts distinct ORDER BY values (peer groups). 1 PRECEDING = previous distinct salary tier.

blocks.label: distribution functions
blocks.code:
-- Percent rank (0 to 1)
SELECT 
  name,
  salary,
  PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary) AS pct_rank,
  CUME_DIST() OVER (ORDER BY salary) AS cume_dist
FROM employees;

-- PERCENT_RANK = (rank - 1) / (total - 1)
-- CUME_DIST = rank / total  (includes ties)

-- Percentile aggregates (ordered-set aggregates)
SELECT 
  percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) AS median,
  percentile_disc(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) AS median_discrete,
  percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) AS p95
FROM employees;
blocks.py-pandas:
# Percent rank
df['pct_rank'] = df['salary'].rank(pct=True)

# Cume dist
df['cume_dist'] = df['salary'].rank(method='max') / len(df)

# Percentiles
df['salary'].quantile([0.5, 0.95])

items.q: PERCENT_RANK vs CUME_DIST for value at position 3 of 10:
items.explain: PERCENT_RANK = (rank-1)/(N-1). CUME_DIST = rank/N. For rank 3 of 10: (3-1)/9=0.22 vs 3/10=0.3.
percentile_cont interpolates between values for exact percentile.
